- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.75) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate when sentiment is low (<0.33) — add 2–5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion bias.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delays) are overpredicted — adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day lagged true values.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment was high.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.75), reduce forecast variance — use 3–5 day moving average smoothing.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–4% to avoid momentum bias.
- High sentiment + low recent price = overconfident model — reduce forecast by 3–5% to reflect caution.
- If sentiment history shows 2+ consecutive high values (>0.75), forecast should be capped at 10% below true peak to avoid overcorrection.
